title: Fleet readiness rhythm — weekly scout notes
content:
Purpose
Quick working notes from this week’s Fleet Readiness Rhythm. Informal capture — decisions, experiment sketches, ops playbook gaps we hit. Use for sync discussion Monday standup (ops channel) and to seed next week’s capacity grooming.

Attendance
- Aisha (owner)
- Miguel (oncall lead)
- Claire (region ops)
- Lena (capacity planning)
- Devon (release-eng/priming infra)

Executive snapshot (TL;DR)
- Overall fleet healthy but regional priming gaps in APAC-SG and EU-CENTRAL for medium-seq workloads.
- Preemption rate on opportunistic pool rose to 4.8% during midday burst on 2029-05-15 — backfill latency increased token cost ~+12% for affected requests.
- US-WEST steady; measured 95th latency for generation routes (gpt-7-mini) 210ms.
- Experiment: targeted prefix-KV prewarm cut cold-start p99 by ~28% in controlled run. Need broader A/B to validate across models.

Region snapshots
US-WEST
- Notes: steady, no new incidents. Increased background compaction for cache nodes on 5/16 caused brief CPU spikes on control plane (observed 03:14-03:26 UTC) — no customer impact.
- Capacity: util at 67% avg; can absorb 15% burst for next 48h.
- Action: postpone non-critical maintenance scheduled 5/20 to keep buffer. Owner: Miguel.

EU-CENTRAL
- Notes: two medium-seq lanes experienced higher queueing 5/15-5/16. Root cause suspected: autoscaler not triggering quickly on MIG node spin-up due to image pull timeouts from internal registry.
- Capacity: util at 78% peak. Serrated usage patterns midday.
- Immediate mitigation: enable short-lived warm pool (30m) for medium-seq profile. Temporary until registry fixes. Owner: Claire.
- Follow-up: INFRA-6048 tracks registry pull timeout fix.

APAC-SG
- Notes: priming effectiveness lower than expected for ops that route to quantized variants. Measured priming hit-rate 32% vs target 60%.
- Likely contributor: mismatch between request fingerprinting hash and actual prefix cache key (edge-case with trimmed user metadata).
- Action: add conservative fingerprint fallback (strip-metadata) in routing proxy. Quick patch scheduled for 5/18. Owner: Devon.

Opportunistic/preemptible pool behavior
- Observed: 4.8% preempt on 5/15 during sustained load; backfill latency bumped token cost for those sessions ~12% (model: vicuna-70b-q4).
- Notes: backfill strategy currently migrates to next-price-tier GPU which sometimes sits in different region -> cross-region cold boot penalty (KV warm lost).
- Suggestion: test local intra-region fallback policy that prefers same-region reserved nodes even if higher cost; simulate cost/latency trade-offs in perf-lab. Owner: Lena + Miguel.

Priming experiment snapshot (KV/prefix caching)
- Small controlled run on 5/16: 1000 requests median seq=512; prefetched KV cache on dedicated warmers reduced cold-start p99 from 1.8s to 1.3s for gpt-7-mini.
- Notes: implementation is memory-heavy; need to estimate global mem footprint if we scale warmers to 2x traffic. Rough calc: 2GB per warmer * 150 warmers = 300GB.
- Next steps: bench memory vs hit-rate curve, prepare cost memo for Product. Owner: Devon.

Risk matrix (short)
- Registry image pull timeouts (EU-CENT): medium severity — affects autoscale speed. Mitigation: warm pool + registry mirroring.
- Cross-region fallback churn: high severity for latency-sensitive apps — mitigation: intra-region fallback policy + prewarmed spare pool.
- Priming mem footprint: low-medium — cost impact but direct QoS upside.

Decisions and proposals
- Approve temporary 30m warm pool for EU-CENT until registry fix (approve now, retro review in two weeks).
- Run intra-region fallback simulation next Wednesday; if simulation shows <8% unit-cost delta with >40% p99 improvement for affected customers, adopt by policy.

Open questions / notes-to-self
- How many customers would see meaningful UX improvement from prioritized intra-region fallbacks? Product to provide top-10 routes by latency sensitivity. (Assigned: Claire)
- Should we surface priming hit-rate to Console per-route? UX cost vs signal fidelity. (PO sync)
- What is acceptable warm-pool memory budget across regions? Finance wants estimates before approving sustained memory increase. (Lena to mock numbers)

Action items (owner / due)
- Miguel: postpone US-WEST maintenance to 5/24; confirm buffer capacity (+ note in runbook). Due 2029-05-18.
- Claire: enable 30m warm pool in EU-CENT; monitor registry pull error rate and autoscaler latency. Due 2029-05-18.
- Devon: push routing proxy patch for fingerprint fallback to canary 5/18; collect priming hit-rate delta. Due 2029-05-19.
- Lena + Miguel: run intra-region fallback cost/latency sim and present numbers in Fri sync. Due 2029-05-22.
- Aisha: draft brief for Product on priming mem footprint and potential billing implications. Due 2029-05-20.

Retro notes (what worked)
- Canary lane for priming experiment was easy to iterate on — good scaffolding.
- Cross-team quick huddle reduced time-to-mitigation on EU-CENT auto-scaler spike.

Retro notes (what didn't)
- Observability gap: we lacked a single dashboard correlating registry pull failures with autoscaler events — had to stitch logs across three systems. Action: create correlation dashboard query in Grafana. (Owner: Claire)

Misc / scratch
- Quick perf numbers: p50/p95/p99 for generation (gpt-7-mini) US-WEST last 24h: 68ms / 160ms / 210ms. EU-CENT: 95ms / 220ms / 1.32s (spiky). APAC-SG: 120ms / 350ms / 1.9s (priming gaps).
- Cost note: opportunistic preempt churn inflated token cost for affected sessions by ~12% — need to check billing attribution (are we absorbing or passing through?). (Finance sync)
- Slack refs: #ops-fleet thread 5/16 "eu autoscale flch" ; #infra-priming 5/16.

Meeting cadence / next checkpoints
- Follow-up sync Fri 2029-05-18 10:30 PT — quick status and numbers.
- Deep-dive priming review Wed 2029-05-22 14:00 PT — include Product & Finance for cost tradeoffs.

Endnotes
- This doc is working capture. Please add inline comments and update action items if you take ownership.
- If anything here needs to be escalated to ENG leadership, flag in the Friday sync.

summary: Weekly working capture for fleet readiness focusing on priming, regional hotspots, and opportunistic pool behavior.
